set.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal Davis-Bacon applies by rule: 24 CFR 983.153(c)(2) requires the owner and its contractors to pay Davis-Bacon wages for PBV development (new construction or rehabilitation under an AHAP) involving nine or more contract units, whether or not completed in stages. PBVs attached to existing housing are not development and do not trigger it. State prevailing wage depends on the other public funds in the deal under Labor Code 1720. https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153

reason: 24 CFR 983.153(c)(2) applies Davis-Bacon to PBV development of nine or more contract units.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: DIR Decision on Administrative Appeal, PW 2006-020 Heber Family Apartments (April 5, 2007), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe Village and PW 2006-005 Central Village Apartments, holds that loans of tax-exempt conduit bond proceeds for affordable housing, whether publicly offered or privately placed, are not a payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(1) and are not a public below-market loan under 1720(b)(4), because the proceeds and repayments never enter public coffers; reaffirmed in PW 2010-008 and PW 2015-008. Bond financing alone does not trigger state prevailing wage; other public funds in the same deal (city or county loans, fee waivers, land) are tested separately, and federal sources such as HOME or 9+ PBVs carry their own Davis-Bacon rules. https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf

reason: DIR PW 2006-020 holds conduit bond loans for affordable housing are not public funds under Labor Code 1720(b).

set.prevailing_wage_basis: Only general rule found: Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats fees waived or reduced by a political subdivision as payment out of public funds, but the outcome depends on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts (the 1720(c)(3) de minimis test of under $600,000 and under 2 percent of project cost may exempt small waivers; the 1720(c)(5)(E) exemption covers below-market loans, not fee waivers). No City ordinance, resolution or DIR determination on point was found. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
set.audit_note: Prevailing wage left unclear: basis is only Labor Code 1720(b)(4) and depends on waiver size and other public funds in the deal.

reason: No stated rule beyond Labor Code 1720(b)(4); searched Labor Code 1720, DIR coverage determinations and Chula Vista fee waiver resolutions.
